residuals.title: Trusted deployers and load-time module code
residuals.statement: Someone who can change packages or deployment configuration can defeat in-process controls (TH-G02-001, TH-G02-069). The deployment lock detects drift from the reviewed release, but module assemblies load before it is verified, so code that runs at load time is not stopped, and the lock binds manifests and listed files only, not the host's own assemblies.

residuals.title: Composition switches and module disabling
residuals.statement: Composition switches are not recorded in or checked against the lock (FND-001), and disabling a module with a report of its dependents, running work and retained data (FND-003) is not built. Under the restart model a selection that drops a required module is refused at composition.
residuals.owner: No G-02 work order; DEV-005 tooling at G-06

residuals.title: Host, container and recovery evidence
residuals.statement: The evidence for these controls runs in test hosts over real PostgreSQL and the filesystem provider. Evidence on the sample host and its container, including lifecycle, migration, key-ring and audit recovery, is CODE-10's and is not part of this map.

residuals.title: Extension properties are not built
residuals.statement: No extension-property mechanism exists, so there is nothing for TM-G02-005 to govern and no test evidences it. A module that adds extension properties must arrive with their sensitivity and permission declarations and the tests of this control.

residuals.title: Request-time limits and declared-field paging
residuals.statement: Request size, structure and header limits are enforced and tested, but whole-request time limits, JSON field lengths, and bounded paging, sorting and filtering on declared fields are partly built and not evidenced. The fixture endpoints bound their own pages.

residuals.title: Refusals before the application pipeline
residuals.statement: The host-filtering 400 for an unconfigured host and Kestrel's own refusals, such as 431, come before the application pipeline: they carry no problem body, no HSTS and no nosniff header, and a host without UseModularynApi answers ingress refusals with bare status codes. AC-004-N01 observes the bare 400, which reveals nothing.

residuals.title: Secrets in module code and release artifacts
residuals.statement: Secret types keep secrets out of what the framework formats and logs, but cannot stop module code from logging a revealed value or placing one in an exception. That a secret setting accepts only replacement is not evidenced, release artifacts are not scanned for secrets, and a secret store's own startup refusal names the secret it could not read.

residuals.title: Provider compatibility and settings reload
residuals.statement: Typed configuration is validated before readiness, but provider compatibility, such as the PostgreSQL server version, is checked only by the test harness, and validation before an application or tenant settings reload takes effect is not built; deployment options take effect only at restart.

residuals.title: Key ring at rest and key-management policy
residuals.statement: The data-protection key ring is stored unencrypted in an owner-only directory, whose access control is its only protection. Application code can still register another key manager, add escrow sinks or turn off rotation after the declaration, the declaration keeps one store per options scope without removing them, and the separate backup of the ring is an untested operational procedure.
residuals.owner: No G-02 work order; backup procedure at G-08

residuals.title: HSTS choices are not recorded with the release
residuals.statement: HTTPS redirection and HSTS are emitted and tested, but the deployment's subdomain and preload choices are not recorded with the release.

residuals.title: Shared capacity and within-tenant availability
residuals.statement: G-02 has no per-tenant quotas: request bounds and quota reservation limit single requests and one tenant's temporary storage, not its share of the host (TH-G02-070). Within a tenant, one member can hold every read slot or pending upload place; TenantCache has no size bound, and cache outage behaviour (AC-030) is outside G-02.

residuals.title: Weak passwords
residuals.statement: Adaptive hashing raises the cost of guessing a stolen verifier but cannot protect a password that is easy to guess (TH-G02-072).

residuals.title: Throttling and sign-in availability
residuals.statement: Delays and source blocking keep an attacker from locking an account indefinitely, but several sources acting together keep a targeted user's sign-in slowed for as long as they fail (TH-G02-076), and no operator alert exists. A reverse proxy that is not declared collapses its clients into one source, timing uniformity was measured on loopback only, and throttle rows accumulate until retention removes them.
residuals.owner: No G-02 work order for an operator alert

residuals.title: Key separation for seeds and passkeys
residuals.statement: Encrypted one-time-password seeds and integrity-tagged passkey records stay protected only while their keys are held apart from the database; a compromise that reaches both exposes them (TH-G02-073, TH-G02-075).
residuals.owner: Accepted at G-02 qualification; restore evidence with CODE-10 and OPS-004

residuals.title: Credential journeys are G-03's
residuals.statement: G-02 delivers the stored forms of one-time-password seeds, recovery codes and passkey records with their tests. Enrolment, verification, recovery and passkey registration and sign-in, and the limits on those codes at an entry point, are G-03's journeys.

residuals.title: Administrator-issued delegation and impersonation
residuals.statement: Delegation that the subject grants is built and tested; delegation or impersonation issued by an administrator is specified by no G-02 work order and is not built. Its existing evidence is ExecutionPrincipal's separation of actor and effective subject, with identity kind, which every decision and audit record uses; G-03 must build the journey on it.

residuals.title: Client credential providers
residuals.statement: The origin-bound credential provider is built and tested; generated and dynamic clients that ask it for every request and refuse redirects off its origin are not driven end to end, and no upload can be client-visible until clients model an upload's body.

residuals.title: Freshness window
residuals.statement: Within the declared freshness bound a revoked grant or session can still act (TH-G02-020, TH-G02-040): under the bounded profile another process sees a change only within the bound. Security-sensitive permissions are decided at the current profile.

residuals.title: Module code is trusted in process
residuals.statement: Module code runs in process with the host's authority. Code that opens the connection itself can run any SQL past every filter, reflection can build the adapter's markers and internal constructors, and owner-bound rules rest on a source check. Server code that builds a session-scheme claims principal can establish a member context for any member; since SEC-08 it gives a service identity no authority there. A handler that casts the request's IHttpResponseFeature to IHttpResponseBodyFeature, which is the server's own object, writes a response of any media type past the media-type check that every supported write path passes. The query guard depends on EF Core 10.0.14's query shapes.
residuals.owner: None: the module trust model; every EF Core upgrade reruns the query-guard tests

residuals.title: What a host operation reached
residuals.statement: The framework audits each host scope's grant, with its actor, operation and reason, and each cross-tenant read with its entity and grant, before the access. Which tenants an operation affected is recorded only if the operation's module records it, as the AC-004-N03 fixture does. Including tenant navigations from a host scope is untested, and a tenant's invalidation does not reach host-scope entries that aggregate it, which their staleness bound limits.

residuals.title: The principal inside authorized work
residuals.statement: AuthorizedWorkRunner decides for the principal its caller passes, but the work runs in a new scope whose principal accessor holds nothing, so module code that resolves the accessor there sees no principal and is refused. The Authorization README states that a step must pass the principal it was given; what remains is that the runner does not set the accessor, so code that relies on it fails closed rather than acting.

residuals.title: Member invitations are G-03's
residuals.statement: Tenant administrators cannot add members until G-03's invitation flow; memberships change only through identity's audited host operations, and G-03 must lead from a tenant-level decision to that write without implicit host scope.

residuals.title: Entitlements and plans are G-03's
residuals.statement: Permissions, settings, features and composition are kept separate and tested; entitlements and plans do not exist until G-03, where they attach at the feature gate.

residuals.title: Data at rest
residuals.statement: Content encryption under FND-031 is not enabled, so file content, records and audit rows are stored unencrypted, and the slice relies on host and database access controls: a host or database compromise exposes Confidential and Restricted data.
residuals.owner: A later work order (FND-031), as the operator decided

residuals.title: Scanner limits
residuals.statement: Files has no content scanner: release runs the deployment's policy, and the opt-in allowlist policy makes no file safe, since a released document can still carry an exploit or script. Detection recognizes known patterns, so novel content can pass (TH-G02-049).
residuals.owner: Accepted at G-02 qualification; each deployment's release policy

residuals.title: Already delivered data
residuals.statement: Revocation stops new access through the gateway but cannot recall files or responses already delivered.

residuals.title: No anonymous file delivery
residuals.statement: Every download needs a signed-in session, as the operator decided for G-02; the bounded-bearer profile for public files is gate W's.

residuals.title: Files edge cases
residuals.statement: Under invariant globalization a file name is checked as given, without normalization; active grants per tenant are not capped; one spare-bits token case is not exercised by its test; and scheduled recovery waits on the job runtime.
residuals.owner: No owner named; CODE-05 for scheduled recovery

residuals.title: Audit integrity
residuals.statement: Append-only is enforced by the persistence adapter, not by the database, so a database administrator or the schema owner can alter or delete audit rows, and no tamper evidence is claimed (TH-G02-060).

residuals.title: A sealed reference does not bind its row's payload, kind or state
residuals.statement: The seal binds a stored reference to its row's identity and its store's purpose. A writer with direct database access can therefore requeue a row, or change its payload or kind, and it runs again under the same reference. AC-004-N03 shows each such run stays in the producer's revalidated tenant and within its current authority, and stops once that authority is revoked. The Reviewer judged stating it acceptable for G-02, since a direct database writer is already outside the model's trust boundary, as RR-G02-029 accepts for audit rows, and asked that it be revisited when payloads gain external effects (RR-G02-041).
residuals.owner: The operator's decision (see the control map README)

residuals.title: Scrubber and payload rule limits
residuals.statement: The scrubber and the payload rule recognize secret forms, now including a secret reference, behind the allowlisted-fields rule; a password or a secret's value that a module logs or places in a payload has no recognizable form and is not caught. Nothing yet runs quarantined-payload redaction or receipt pruning on its own.
residuals.owner: No owner named; a maintenance runner later

residuals.title: No operator endpoints for audit, diagnostics and lag
residuals.statement: Audit and diagnostics reads are authorized and tested as services, but no HTTP endpoint exposes them, and durable work's lag is not exposed to operators.
residuals.owner: A later API order under CODE-06's inventory

residuals.title: Access records precede the access
residuals.statement: Records of access, such as a host-scope grant, a filter bypass or an audit read, are written in their own transaction before the access, so a record can exist for an access that then failed; a soft-deleted read in a named deployment scope is not recorded.

residuals.title: Durable work needs the declared key ring
residuals.statement: A host must declare SEC-02's key ring for any durable work, or no reference is stored and work defers; references of format 1 are no longer read, which is safe only because nothing has been released.

residuals.title: Correlation without the API conventions
residuals.statement: A host without UseModularynApi decides correlation after the ingress and so adopts no declared proxy's trace context.

residuals.title: Composition roots outside the samples
residuals.statement: DEP014 gives sample hosts a composition-root role, and DEP015 refuses references between test projects; a composition-root role for applications built on Modularyn outside the samples is left to a later order.
residuals.owner: A later work order, as the operator decided

residuals.title: Sign-in posts JSON
residuals.statement: Identity's sign-in endpoint accepts JSON only, so a sample's sign-in page posts with a small same-origin script that fetches its antiforgery token, not with a plain HTML form.

residuals.title: Evidence on fixture endpoints rather than every shipped surface
residuals.statement: Safe methods that change nothing, strict input contracts, conflict responses and browser cross-site behaviour are evidenced on the fixture modules' declared endpoints, through a verified browser, not on every shipped endpoint or the sample's pages; no G-02 interface renders permission-dependent controls, and the AC-002 and AC-012 acceptance families have no tests here.
residuals.owner: CODE-06 and CODE-09; the AC-002 and AC-012 families outside the G-02 plan

residuals.title: Contract evolution against the previous release
residuals.statement: Breaking changes are detected against the committed baseline; no comparison with the previous release's contract, consumer migration gate or detection of meaning-only changes exists.

residuals.title: No tenant-configurable declaration for settings
residuals.statement: Deployment options are separate from settings and cannot be overridden by a tenant, which AC-003-N03 shows; but a setting has no declaration that it is tenant-configurable, so a tenant holding the management permission can override any declared setting.
residuals.owner: A later settings work order, which must add a tenant-configurable declaration to setting definitions and refuse a tenant's override of any setting that lacks it

residuals.title: Idempotent external effects from events
residuals.statement: Consumers deduplicate and order delivery, and API mutations take idempotency keys; no G-02 event handler performs an external effect, so idempotency keys for such effects are unevidenced.
residuals.owner: The first module with an external effect

residuals.title: Client-visible values have no audience
residuals.statement: A value is client-visible to every member of its tenant or to none. A value visible only to an administrator is a user-scope override, as AC-004-B02 prepares it, or a value served through an authorized endpoint.

residuals.title: Return addresses may name any configured origin
residuals.statement: Sign-in accepts a local path or any configured public origin as its return address, another tenant's domain included; the request that follows is resolved and refused there like any other, and no Host or forwarded value is ever used.

residuals.title: Test browser and package provenance
residuals.statement: The pinned Chrome Headless Shell archives' SHA-256 values rest on Playwright's CDN and Google serving identical bytes, since neither publishes a hash, and their third-party licenses were not reviewed one by one. dotnet nuget verify --all verified Microsoft.Playwright 1.64.1's Microsoft author signature and nuget.org repository countersignature, with their timestamps, without error. It failed only System.ComponentModel.Annotations 5.0.0, signed in 2020: both signatures' validity periods have expired (NU3037), and the local trust store explicitly distrusts both timestamps' Symantec chain (NU3028). Restore still gates both packages on the lock's content hashes, and both packages match nuget.org's catalog SHA-512.

residuals.title: Personal data has no recognized form
residuals.statement: Personal data outside the recognized secret forms is not recognized by redaction or by the payload rule; only producers' choice of references keeps it out, and a per-kind privacy classification needs a manifest or contract change.
residuals.owner: A later manifest or contract change
